What Makes Abacus Global Management, Inc. (ABX) a New Buy Stock

B. Riley Securities named Abacus Global Management its top investment opportunity in the financial services sector, citing expansion into new business lines, growing assets under management and potential for stronger recurring revenue. The firm rates Abacus Buy with a $16 price target. 
Abacus focuses on life insurance as an alternative asset class for institutional and private wealth clients. B. Riley highlighted the expansion of its Abacus Asset Group, securitization and consolidation of acquired policies into income funds, and development of a private wealth platform. 
Abacus raised $378 million across longevity funds and ETFs in Q1 2026, while fee-paying AUM reached $3.28 billion, up 21% from year-end 2024. The company targets more than $5 billion in AUM by the end of 2026. 
B. Riley expects a second securitization and planned interval fund to broaden distribution and support further AUM growth.

@MarketPro $APLD $RILY $BW  The $2M figure needs context. That’s APLD’s ASC 321 carrying value for an illiquid 10% stake—not a market valuation of Base or evidence the stake is worth only $2M. 
 
Same with the note: Base owes APLD the money, not the reverse. The facility permits up to $100M, but principal outstanding at August 31 was $58.5M. “Up to $100M” alone makes the funded exposure sound larger than it was. 
 
The real catalyst is the BW guarantee: a Base exchange listing will let APLD terminate its backstop on a $2.4B project by giving notice. That is huge. 
 
The way I see this: APLD’s Base stake is the upside; the power contract is the strategy; the guarantee is the risk. The IPO could change all three. 
 
So yes, APLD’s relationship with Base is much bigger than a $2M carrying value suggests. But you have to distinguish an investment from a loan receivable, and a contingent guarantee from funded debt.

Wow, the $RILY $APLD  Base Electron $BW trade just got a lot more interesting. 
 
Base Electron has confidentially filed for an IPO. Read the actual $APLD  guarantee: once Base’s common stock is approved for trading on a national exchange, APLD can terminate its guarantee of Base’s obligations under BW’s $2.4B power project by delivering notice to BW. The release even covers liabilities that accrued before notice. 
 
That is a potential balance-sheet catalyst hiding in plain sight. APLD helped launch the project, received 10% of Base, and could end up owning a stake in a public power company while shedding a massive contingent obligation. 
 
For BW, the IPO could mean a better-capitalized customer, though APLD’s backstop would disappear. For $RILY, the read-through is its BW exposure.  
 
The filing alone does not trigger release. Watch the public S-1, the listing entity, exchange approval, and APLD’s notice. If those pieces fall into place, this is far more than another AI-power headline.

@MarketPro $APLD $RILY $BW  The $2M figure needs context. That’s APLD’s ASC 321 carrying value for an illiquid 10% stake—not a market valuation of Base or evidence the stake is worth only $2M. 
 
Same with the note: Base owes APLD the money, not the reverse. The facility permits up to $100M, but principal outstanding at August 31 was $58.5M. “Up to $100M” alone makes the funded exposure sound larger than it was. 
 
The real catalyst is the BW guarantee: a Base exchange listing will let APLD terminate its backstop on a $2.4B project by giving notice. That is huge. 
 
The way I see this: APLD’s Base stake is the upside; the power contract is the strategy; the guarantee is the risk. The IPO could change all three. 
 
So yes, APLD’s relationship with Base is much bigger than a $2M carrying value suggests. But you have to distinguish an investment from a loan receivable, and a contingent guarantee from funded debt.

Wow, the $RILY $APLD  Base Electron $BW trade just got a lot more interesting. 
 
Base Electron has confidentially filed for an IPO. Read the actual $APLD  guarantee: once Base’s common stock is approved for trading on a national exchange, APLD can terminate its guarantee of Base’s obligations under BW’s $2.4B power project by delivering notice to BW. The release even covers liabilities that accrued before notice. 
 
That is a potential balance-sheet catalyst hiding in plain sight. APLD helped launch the project, received 10% of Base, and could end up owning a stake in a public power company while shedding a massive contingent obligation. 
 
For BW, the IPO could mean a better-capitalized customer, though APLD’s backstop would disappear. For $RILY, the read-through is its BW exposure.  
 
The filing alone does not trigger release. Watch the public S-1, the listing entity, exchange approval, and APLD’s notice. If those pieces fall into place, this is far more than another AI-power headline.

Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: $UNCY ) has appointed Meredith Manning, M.B.A., to its Board of Directors, where she will serve on the Audit, Compensation, and Nominating and Corporate Governance Committees and will chair the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. 
 
Unicycive Therapeutics, Inc. is a B2i Digital Featured Company. See the company's in-depth profile at: https://b2idigital.com/unicycive-therapeutics 
 
Ms. Manning has more than 25 years of global biopharmaceutical experience, including commercial leadership roles at three companies: 
 
• As Chief Commercial Officer of Soleno Therapeutics, Inc., she built the commercial organization from inception and led the U.S. launch of VYKAT™ XR, the first FDA-approved treatment for hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome 
 
• As General Manager, and later, President, The Americas, of PharmaEssentia Corporation, she built the U.S. organization and led the U.S. commercial launch of BESREMi® 
 
• At Shire (formerly Baxter/Baxalta), she led a seven-brand portfolio across more than 65 countries 
 
Regarding Ms. Manning's role as Unicycive advances oxylanthanum carbonate (OLC), Shalabh Gupta, M.D., Chief Executive Officer of Unicycive Therapeutics, said: "We look forward to benefiting from Meredith’s strategic insight and first-hand experience as we advance OLC towards potential approval and prepare for the next stage of the Company’s growth."

Unicycive Therapeutics is a biotechnology company developing novel treatments for kidney diseases. Unicycive’s lead investigational treatment is oxylanthanum carbonate, a novel phosphate binding agent for the treatment of hyperphosphatemia in patients with chronic kidney disease who are on dialysis. Unicycive’s second investigational treatment UNI-494 is intended for the treatment of conditions related to acute kidney injury. It has been granted orphan drug designation (ODD) by the FDA for the prevention of Delayed Graft Function (DGF) in kidney transplant patients and has completed a Phase 1 dose-ranging safety study in healthy volunteers. $TMUS Elon claiming Starlink’s 800 MHz buy creates a "major carrier" defies physics & market reality.

1/ CapEx & The Swap: $TMUS inherited 800 MHz from Sprint and dumped it. Deploying it meant billions in CapEx mounting heavy gear on thousands of towers for narrow bandwidth they didn't need. TMUS swapped it with Grain for cash + 600 MHz to expand existing 600MHZ gear with zero new CapEx.

2/ Desperation Premium: No carrier sells spectrum to a rival. This was the only nationwide low-band block available to buy. Elon paid an $8B desperation tax for an asset nobody else wanted. 14 MHz is an SOS backup, not a carrier.

3/ Shannon Limit: 14 MHz paired yields ~35–50 Mbps per beam. Shared across hundreds of sq miles, urban mobile broadband is mathematically impossible.

4/ Inverse-Square Law: A phone transmits at 0.2W. Overcoming ~180 dB path loss through concrete, glass, and 300 miles to orbit is impossible indoors. 0.2W can’t talk back from inside.
